architecture_tree.name: WFF Engineering Lifecycle System
architecture_tree.responsibility: Coordinate evidence-linked software lifecycle work for AI agents through bounded routes, phase handoffs, support capabilities, and claim ceilings.
non_responsibilities: It does not replace product, architecture, implementation, or acceptance judgment with one deterministic script.
architecture_tree.rationale: The product description and control matrix consistently define a lifecycle framework whose value comes from decomposition, handoff, and evidence rather than one monolithic generator.

architecture_tree.name: Admission and Route Control
architecture_tree.responsibility: Determine whether work enters WFF, which external route applies, and whether downstream continuation has an accepted WFF-native handoff.
non_responsibilities: It does not create missing product or architecture truth while routing.
architecture_tree.rationale: The router skill names exactly three external routes and separates them from internal continuation routes.

architecture_tree.name: External Entry Routing
architecture_tree.responsibility: Route rough material to requirements intake, stable demand to formal P1, and code-backed existing systems to PhaseX.
non_responsibilities: It does not expose P2, P3, or P4 as direct external entry routes.
architecture_tree.rationale: The external route table explicitly binds input state to wff-req-chat, wff-req, or wff-x.

architecture_tree.name: Accepted Handoff Continuation
architecture_tree.responsibility: Permit P2, P3, and P4 only when their required WFF-native upstream artifacts and evidence are accepted.
non_responsibilities: It does not promote standalone non-WFF documents into accepted downstream truth.
architecture_tree.rationale: The continuation table explicitly requires accepted P1, P2, and P3 handoff surfaces.

architecture_tree.name: P1-P4 Greenfield Mainline
architecture_tree.responsibility: Move accepted demand through requirements, architecture, implementation, and validation closure with explicit handoffs and evidence.
non_responsibilities: It does not treat mechanical completion of every phase as production approval.
architecture_tree.rationale: The orientation map names the P1-P4 mainline and the downstream phase skills define their distinct ownership.

architecture_tree.name: Pre-P1 Requirements Intake
architecture_tree.responsibility: Turn rough ideas and mixed source material into a truth-state-marked P1 source brief and admission decision.
non_responsibilities: It does not generate the official PRD or claim P1 completion.
architecture_tree.rationale: wff-req-chat declares itself a pre-Phase-1 intake and explicitly rejects PRD authority.

architecture_tree.name: Phase 1 Product Requirements
architecture_tree.responsibility: Own product truth, business pressure, scope, acceptance intent, and the design handoff while preserving source authority and visible gaps.
non_responsibilities: It does not decide architecture, database, code, or implementation plan.
architecture_tree.rationale: The official P1 skill states its truth authority and evidence-capped boundary, and the committed runner implements source admission, orchestration, and gate-command construction.

architecture_tree.name: Phase 2 Design and Architecture
architecture_tree.responsibility: Translate accepted P1 truth into architecture boundaries, risk posture, data/API contracts, and implementation-facing handoff.
non_responsibilities: It does not rediscover product truth or treat machine pass as architecture value.
architecture_tree.rationale: The P2 entry names architecture ownership and requires P1 truth as upstream authority; the runtime implements source admission, the mainline, and claim-control sidecars.

architecture_tree.name: Phase 3 Implementation Delivery
architecture_tree.responsibility: Turn accepted P2 contracts into bounded runnable implementation, tests, runtime evidence, and delivery handoff.
non_responsibilities: It does not invent missing product or architecture truth or equate script pass with delivery readiness.
architecture_tree.rationale: The P3 entry explicitly requires accepted P2 input, bounded packages, prior failing tests, and weakest-evidence claim capping; the runtime implements source admission, mainline execution, and generated-output contamination checks.

architecture_tree.name: Phase 4 Validation Closure
architecture_tree.responsibility: Read upstream delivery evidence, judge closure under a claim ceiling, and route defects to their owning phase with a minimum rerun boundary.
non_responsibilities: It does not mutate upstream artifacts, repair missing truth, or grant production approval without external evidence.
architecture_tree.rationale: The P4 entry defines read-only validation, review-bound missing evidence, explicit production exclusions, and ownership routing; the runner implements source admission, mainline execution, and claim-control emission.

architecture_tree.name: PhaseX Brownfield Assessment
architecture_tree.responsibility: Establish code-backed current-system facts, uncertainty, compatibility constraints, risks, safety nets, and an honest re-entry route.
non_responsibilities: It is not a default phase after P4 and does not accept standalone documents as system truth.
architecture_tree.rationale: The PhaseX skill defines itself as a code-backed side route and requires fact/inference/unknown separation plus safety-net planning; the validator distinguishes authored-valid cases and rejects legacy PX-SK surfaces.

architecture_tree.name: Shared Lifecycle Support
architecture_tree.responsibility: Provide reusable project context, traceability, reader translation, and interaction-map capabilities consumed across routes and phases.
non_responsibilities: Support capabilities do not become new lifecycle phases or content-truth owners.
architecture_tree.rationale: The skill catalog and install-profile configuration explicitly register these four cross-phase support capabilities and their composition packages.

architecture_tree.name: Durable Project Context
architecture_tree.responsibility: Maintain concise durable project facts, constraints, references, and conflict notes that help agents make cross-task judgments.
non_responsibilities: It does not replace P1-P4/PX truth or silently override human-maintained context.
architecture_tree.rationale: The project-context skill names its maintained artifact, durable-context purpose, non-authoritative status, and conflict-routing behavior.

architecture_tree.name: Artifact Identity and Traceability
architecture_tree.responsibility: Manage canonical IDs, file and anchor bindings, upstream/downstream links, integrity checks, and project-bound derived registry records.
non_responsibilities: It does not replace documents as source truth or derive accepted claims from rendered projections.
architecture_tree.rationale: The traceability skill explicitly separates document meaning from registry identity/link ownership and keeps SQLite derived and project-bound.

architecture_tree.name: Localized Reader Translation
architecture_tree.responsibility: Produce reader-facing localized editions of canonical lifecycle artifacts while preserving technical anchors, facts, decisions, and claim ceilings.
non_responsibilities: It does not replace the canonical source or add validation, UAT, sign-off, or production claims.
architecture_tree.rationale: The reader-translation contract defines a release-facing localized projection with canonical authority and explicit non-escalation rules.

architecture_tree.name: Interaction Map Rendering
architecture_tree.responsibility: Validate and render source-labeled P1/P2 interaction-map packets as deterministic human-review projections.
non_responsibilities: It does not author product or architecture truth, accept evidence, operate a gate, or raise claim ceilings.
architecture_tree.rationale: The interaction-map skill defines an optional rendering companion whose validation is structural and whose renderer owns projection only.

architecture_tree.name: Evidence and Assurance
architecture_tree.responsibility: Capture tests, traces, runtime proof, validation reports, review surfaces, and formal gates that prove or cap claims.
non_responsibilities: Assurance does not create product, architecture, or implementation truth.
architecture_tree.rationale: The governance matrix assigns proof and claim ceilings to Evidence/Gates and explicitly forbids content-truth creation.

architecture_tree.name: AI / External Review Projection
architecture_tree.responsibility: Provide an additive human-readable review entry over canonical artifacts, evidence, risks, and review-bound decisions.
non_responsibilities: It does not replace canonical artifacts, become gate truth, or raise the claim ceiling.
architecture_tree.rationale: The public review-surface contract states that canonical paths remain authoritative and the projection is additive and non-escalating.

architecture_tree.name: Capability Packaging and Distribution
architecture_tree.responsibility: Compose skills and resource modules into install profiles and release packages for specific user or maintainer scenarios.
non_responsibilities: Packaging does not alter lifecycle truth or prove universal standalone installability.
architecture_tree.rationale: The profile configuration organizes capability packages, resource modules, and scenario profiles, while the builder implements profile selection, script dependency closure, and content-policy trimming under governance claim limits.

architecture_tree.name: Role-Agent Adaptation
architecture_tree.responsibility: Export role-oriented entry surfaces that route users back to existing WFF skills, profiles, and evidence boundaries.
non_responsibilities: Role agents do not replace phase responsibility, source truth, architecture truth, implementation truth, or evidence gates.
architecture_tree.rationale: Governance and orientation consistently define role agents as optional adapters rather than a new runtime or methodology.

responsibility_map.subject: Global engineering order
responsibility_map.responsibility: Own lifecycle route selection, stage order, required inputs/outputs, handoff contracts, return paths, repeatable execution, and evidence capture.
non_responsibilities: Generated code and test body content
responsibility_map.rationale: The governing control matrix assigns global order and interfaces to Workflow and excludes content truth.

responsibility_map.subject: Uncertainty and engineering judgment
responsibility_map.responsibility: Interpret source truth, judge context sufficiency, decide product and architecture semantics, author implementation meaning, and perform bounded review judgment.
responsibility_map.rationale: The governing control matrix directly assigns uncertainty and semantic judgment to Agentic reasoning.

responsibility_map.subject: Depth and review guidance
responsibility_map.responsibility: Ask bounded questions, direct output depth, and surface review concerns where agentic work risks becoming shallow.
responsibility_map.rationale: Governance explicitly limits Templates/TVG to direction and depth without answer authority.

responsibility_map.subject: Proof and formal claim state
responsibility_map.responsibility: Prove behavior and execution, expose defects, route failures, and cap formal claims according to available evidence.
non_responsibilities: Equating script pass with product or architecture quality
responsibility_map.rationale: Governance gives Evidence/Gates proof authority but expressly denies content-truth ownership.

responsibility_map.subject: External admission and downstream continuation
responsibility_map.responsibility: Select among requirements intake, formal P1, and code-backed PhaseX, and require accepted upstream artifacts for P2-P4 continuation.
non_responsibilities: Promotion of standalone non-WFF artifacts into accepted truth
responsibility_map.rationale: The route skill defines only three external entries and a separate accepted-handoff continuation table.

responsibility_map.subject: Product requirements truth
responsibility_map.responsibility: Own product truth, business pressure, scope, acceptance intent, source-authority preservation, and design handoff.
responsibility_map.rationale: The P1 skill explicitly names product-truth authority and evidence-capped outputs.

responsibility_map.subject: Architecture and design truth
responsibility_map.responsibility: Own architecture translation, boundaries, risk posture, data/API contracts, dependencies, and implementation handoff from accepted P1 truth.
non_responsibilities: Making machine pass equal architecture value
responsibility_map.rationale: The P2 skill assigns architecture ownership and binds it to accepted P1 authority.

responsibility_map.subject: Runnable implementation delivery
responsibility_map.responsibility: Own bounded implementation packages, tests, runtime evidence, and delivery handoff under accepted P2 contracts.
non_responsibilities: Claiming readiness beyond the weakest evidence
responsibility_map.rationale: The P3 skill requires accepted P2 input, returns upstream on missing truth, and caps claims by evidence.

responsibility_map.subject: Validation closure and remediation routing
responsibility_map.responsibility: Consume upstream evidence read-only, judge validation closure, preserve review-bound gaps, and route defects to the responsible phase.
non_responsibilities: Granting production or owner approval without external proof
responsibility_map.rationale: The P4 skill defines a read-only validation and routing boundary with explicit external-evidence exclusions.

responsibility_map.subject: Existing-system truth and re-entry
responsibility_map.responsibility: Recover code-backed current-state facts, separate uncertainty, identify compatibility risk and safety nets, and recommend the honest P1/P2/P3/protect-first route.
non_responsibilities: Treating standalone documents as system truth
responsibility_map.rationale: The PhaseX skill declares a code-backed side route and explicit fact/uncertainty/safety-net responsibilities.

responsibility_map.subject: Durable project context
responsibility_map.responsibility: Maintain concise cross-task project facts, constraints, reference entry points, and explicit conflict notes in `.wff/PROJECT_CONTEXT.md`.
responsibility_map.rationale: The project-context contract explicitly defines both the maintained surface and its non-authoritative lifecycle boundary.

responsibility_map.subject: Artifact identity and links
responsibility_map.responsibility: Own canonical artifact IDs, file/anchor bindings, dependency links, integrity checks, and a derived project-bound registry.
responsibility_map.rationale: The traceability contract explicitly states that documents own meaning while the registry owns identity, bindings, and link integrity.

responsibility_map.subject: Localized reader editions
responsibility_map.responsibility: Translate canonical lifecycle artifacts into reader-facing localized editions while preserving technical anchors and factual/claim fidelity.
responsibility_map.rationale: The reader-translation contract explicitly keeps canonical authority and forbids claim upgrades.

responsibility_map.subject: Interaction-map validation and rendering
responsibility_map.responsibility: Perform structural packet validation, deterministic layout checks, and mechanical HTML/SVG projection for human review.
responsibility_map.rationale: The interaction-map contract sharply limits its scripts to structure, layout, and mechanical projection.

responsibility_map.subject: Scenario packaging
responsibility_map.responsibility: Compose capability packages, skills, scripts, templates, reference packages, and resource modules for supported scenarios.
responsibility_map.rationale: The configuration explicitly models capability packages and profiles, while governance defines packaging as a supported surface rather than proof of universal independence.

responsibility_map.subject: Human-readable review projection
responsibility_map.responsibility: Project canonical artifacts and evidence into a prioritized review entry while preserving source paths, risks, and review-bound decisions.
responsibility_map.rationale: The review contract repeatedly identifies the surface as additive, read-only, and non-escalating.

responsibility_map.subject: Role-oriented user entry
responsibility_map.responsibility: Expose PM, architect, programmer, QA, and reviewer-style entry surfaces over the existing skill/profile system.
responsibility_map.rationale: Governance and orientation define role agents as optional entry/adaptation surfaces.

implementation_intents.subject: Bounded context instead of monolithic prompting
implementation_intents.statement: WFF is designed to reduce long-context failure by decomposing work into bounded phases and modules whose outputs reconnect through explicit evidence and handoffs.
implementation_intents.rationale: The product README directly explains decomposition and evidence linkage as the mechanism for avoiding context loss, while the route and phase model operationalize that mechanism.

implementation_intents.subject: Source truth remains upstream authority
implementation_intents.statement: Each phase is intended to consume accepted upstream truth, preserve unresolved gaps, and return rather than invent missing product or architecture meaning.
implementation_intents.rationale: P1, P2, and P3 contracts explicitly preserve source authority and require upstream return on missing truth.

implementation_intents.subject: Agentic reasoning owns the semantic middle
implementation_intents.statement: The framework intentionally uses workflow and schemas for order and evidence while reserving uncertain product, architecture, implementation, and review judgment for an agentic layer.
implementation_intents.rationale: The highest project principle and responsibility matrix explicitly divide these control responsibilities.

implementation_intents.subject: Lifecycle contracts are backed by executable boundary controls
implementation_intents.statement: The committed P1-P4 runtime surfaces implement source-admission checks and phase-specific gate, claim-control, or contamination-control paths rather than leaving those boundaries only in prose.
implementation_intents.rationale: The admitted runner implementations contain explicit source-admission functions and concrete gate, claim-control, mainline, or generated-output contamination paths for each phase.

implementation_intents.subject: Implementation progresses through bounded work and evidence
implementation_intents.statement: Phase 3 is intended to freeze accepted contracts, establish failing tests, implement bounded packages, and accumulate differentiated test/runtime/delivery evidence before raising formal state.
implementation_intents.rationale: The P3 entry directly names failing tests, bounded packages, runnable delivery, and weakest-evidence capping.

implementation_intents.subject: Validation is read-only and route-producing
implementation_intents.statement: Phase 4 is intended to consume and judge inherited evidence without silently repairing upstream artifacts, then return deficiencies to the phase that owns them.
implementation_intents.rationale: The P4 contract explicitly defines read-only operation, review-bound missing evidence, and routed remediation ownership.

implementation_intents.subject: Distribution is configuration-led capability composition
implementation_intents.statement: Install packaging is intended to compose stable capability packages and resource modules into scenario-specific profiles without redefining lifecycle semantics.
implementation_intents.rationale: The profile configuration explicitly separates capability packages, profiles, and resource modules, and the public orientation document denies that profiles create a new methodology.

implementation_intents.subject: Human Review is an additive decision surface
implementation_intents.statement: The Human Review lane is intended to make canonical artifacts and evidence easier to judge without becoming a second source of lifecycle, trace, or gate truth.
implementation_intents.rationale: The review contract explicitly preserves canonical paths and labels the dossier as a read-only projection with no claim-ceiling increase.

assurance_ownership.subject: Implementation behavior proof
assurance_ownership.responsibility: Demonstrate behavior, contracts, scenarios, persistence, and bounded runtime outcomes produced by implementation work.
assurance_ownership.rationale: P3 owns runnable implementation and differentiated evidence, while the global matrix assigns proof rather than content truth to Evidence/Gates.

assurance_ownership.subject: Execution claim proof
assurance_ownership.responsibility: Support claims that generated implementation actually executes in the tested environment and expose missing infrastructure or UI evidence.
assurance_ownership.rationale: P3 distinguishes runtime and weakest-evidence boundaries, and WFF describes Harness evidence as execution proof rather than complete delivery truth.

assurance_ownership.subject: Formal state and claim ceiling
assurance_ownership.responsibility: Block, route, or cap formal state based on traces, tests, runtime proof, validation reports, and unresolved defects.
assurance_ownership.rationale: The governing control model directly assigns this authority to Evidence/Gates.

assurance_ownership.subject: Cross-evidence closure judgment
assurance_ownership.responsibility: Aggregate inherited evidence read-only, classify missing proof, determine the bounded closure state, and route remediation.
assurance_ownership.rationale: The P4 contract names read-only validation and explicit routing responsibilities.

assurance_ownership.subject: Independent decision readability
assurance_ownership.owner: AI / external reviewer through Human Review surface
assurance_ownership.responsibility: Help a reviewer inspect canonical decisions, sources, risks, evidence, and review questions without replacing the underlying artifacts or formal gates.
assurance_ownership.rationale: The Human Review contract defines an additive, source-preserving, non-escalating projection.

assurance_ownership.subject: Architecture decision quality
assurance_ownership.owner: Agentic architecture judgment plus review evidence
assurance_ownership.responsibility: Judge architecture trade-offs and unresolved risk while using structural checks and source links as evidence rather than answer generators.
assurance_ownership.rationale: The responsibility matrix assigns architecture trade-offs to Agentic reasoning, P2 limits machine-pass authority, and Evidence/Gates remain proof owners.

constraints.subject: External route boundary
constraints.statement: Only wff-req-chat, wff-req, and wff-x are external WFF entry routes; P2, P3, and P4 require accepted WFF-native upstream artifacts.
constraints.rationale: Both the public README and router skill state this boundary explicitly.

constraints.subject: Deterministic control cannot own semantic truth
constraints.statement: Workflow, templates, schemas, validators, reports, and gates must not replace agentic ownership of uncertain product, architecture, or implementation meaning.
constraints.rationale: The highest project principle and responsibility matrix explicitly prohibit this drift.

constraints.subject: Default release claim ceiling
constraints.statement: Default WFF evidence supports development or pre-production workflow claims, not real UAT, production approval, owner sign-off, go-live, or production risk acceptance unless named external evidence exists.
constraints.rationale: Repository governance and the P4 contract explicitly list excluded production-level claims.

constraints.subject: Role-agent authority ceiling
constraints.statement: Role agents are optional entry/adaptation surfaces and cannot replace phase responsibility, source truth, architecture truth, implementation truth, evidence gates, or claim ceilings.
constraints.rationale: This boundary is explicit in governance and the public orientation map.

constraints.subject: Install-profile authority ceiling
constraints.statement: Install profiles and scenario packages are composition surfaces; they do not define a new lifecycle methodology or prove that every skill is independently installable.
constraints.rationale: Governance and public documentation explicitly constrain profile claims.

constraints.subject: Human Review projection ceiling
constraints.statement: Human Review outputs remain read-only projections over canonical artifacts and cannot replace trace/gate truth or increase claim ceilings.
constraints.rationale: The review contract explicitly states these non-ownership boundaries.

constraints.subject: Brownfield evidence admission
constraints.statement: PhaseX requires code, runtime, or system facts; standalone PRDs, diagrams, API notes, test reports, or other documents are supporting material rather than sufficient current-system truth.
constraints.rationale: The public README and PhaseX contract both define a code-backed assessment boundary.

unknowns.subject: Production readiness and real UAT
unknowns.statement: The v1.6.2 repository evidence inspected by this baseline does not establish real UAT, production approval, go-live readiness, owner sign-off, or production risk acceptance.
unknowns.rationale: Governance explicitly caps default claims below these states; absence of such authority is retained as an unknown rather than inferred success.

unknowns.subject: Authoritative production deployment topology
unknowns.statement: This Phase 1 architecture memory does not establish an authoritative organization-specific production deployment topology, operational ownership model, or live environment inventory.
unknowns.rationale: The selected evidence describes framework routes, capabilities, packaging, and claim controls rather than a deployed production instance.

unknowns.subject: External business and organizational ownership
unknowns.statement: The repository-level architecture evidence does not identify real project-specific business owners, approval authorities, budgets, or production operators for downstream WFF use cases.
unknowns.rationale: WFF defines lifecycle responsibilities and evidence boundaries, but those are not substitutes for external business ownership evidence.

unknowns.subject: Universal standalone skill installability
unknowns.statement: The baseline does not prove that each individual WFF skill can operate as an independently installable unit without its declared support resources and profile composition.
unknowns.rationale: The documented install unit is a complete skill directory plus support resources, and governance explicitly denies universal standalone-installability claims.
